label: copy-phase input n, in the middle of the recall (recall_idx 3-5, >= 2 outputs left)
explanation: Token-specific feature. It fires only in the copy phase and only when the input token is n (99.7% of activation mass), i.e. the model has just fed back an n it copied. It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, and almost never on other inputs. The plain predicate copy-phase & input n gets recall 0.99 but precision 0.23, so position gates it strongly: activations bunch up at recall_idx 3-4 (n was original token 2-3), at absolute t 10-13, with at least 2 outputs still to go. It is weak or silent for an n near the end of the copy or very early (recall_idx <= 2), and in short sequences (L <= 5). Largest activations: L=9 sequences with n at original position 2, fed back at recall_idx 3. When n is repeated, the second consecutive n gets a smaller activation. Remaining false positives are mostly mid-copy n inputs in L=7-8 sequences that stay silent.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: n, 0, w, s, f, 1; least: t, j, a, d) and the token being output (most: 0, n, s, w, 1, f; least: o, k, -, 3); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, t=12, L=9 & t=12.
